proposals.evidence: DEDR 839 explicitly groups Tamil elumpu, Malayalam ellu, Kota elv, Tulu elu and the extended eluvu/elubu series. Survey elumbə, ellə and yeluvə correspond in stem and bone meaning. Badaga ilə and Betta Kurumba yaləvə are comparative extensions to lects absent from this article; the source annotation identifies the same family but does not make them literal DEDR attestations. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3559 gives the tōl/tokku skin/bark family with Gondi tōla bark, Kodagu tōlï skin, Gadaba tōl skin/bark, Tamil tōl skin and Toda twï·s̱ skin. Source cognacy explicitly identifies the article. Betta Kurumba tōlə is a comparative extension noted as a look-alike by the source; Gadaba tal and Toda tūrs preserve their survey vowel/consonant differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5024 directly gives Tamil/Malayalam mūkku, Kota mūk, Kodagu mūkï, Kurukh muĩ and Parji muvāḍ nose. Source annotations identify this article. Badaga, Betta Kurumba and Ravula mūkə/mūkkə are comparative extensions to lects not listed there; no exact DEDR attestation is claimed for them. Parji nasal-vowel spelling muvãḍ is preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3986(a) documents the pal tooth family: Kodagu pallï, Malayalam pallu, Tamil pal, Malto palu, Kolami pal, Gadaba pal/pallū with plural palkīl, and Toda pas̱. Survey plural and final-vowel material (including palku, pālkill, pāldu) remains unchanged. Toda parse is a comparative correspondence to its distinctive s̱ reflex; Betta Kurumba pallə extends the comparison to a lect absent from this article. Subsection (b) toothstick compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1207 gives Malayalam kattuka/kattikka kindle/burn and Kota kat- burn. Survey katikkuga and kāto retain their morphological/transcription differences. Betta Kurumba kattu is a comparative extension, explicitly only a look-alike in the upstream annotation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
